paras: The shooting of Price Hartgrave took place on July 4, 1919, in Brooklyn, New York, when a police officer shot Hartgrave, 30, after a raid on a crap game. Police said he had attacked an officer with a blade; his friends said he was dragged from his home and shot while held. The Chicago Defender printed both versions, the second as part of a charge of police brutality toward Black residents of the neighborhood.
According to Hartgrave's friends, police had recently been "unusually brutal to Race people" around Dean Street and had been waiting for a chance at Hartgrave.

The police account, as given in a short Brooklyn item, said that Officer Pasquale Dumon shot a man printed as "Prince Hargrave" during a raid on a game after one of the players attacked him with a knife. A fuller dispatch put the shooting in front of 1825 Dean Street and gave the police charge as a razor and a slashed detective.

Hartgrave's friends told a different story. In their version the players scattered when a plain-clothes man approached, and Hartgrave went home. Police then broke in a door, dragged him about three houses down the street, and shot him while two men held him; he was not resisting arrest, they said, and had no razor. They also claimed he was clubbed after he was shot.

As of July 11 Hartgrave was in serious condition in St. John's hospital, although the police-version item named the Bushwick hospital. The cut-off end of the dispatch indicates the matter went to the Police Commissioner. No report of an investigation, charges against the officer, or Hartgrave's recovery appears in the coverage.

The only coverage found is in the Chicago Defender of July 12, 1919, from its Brooklyn correspondent. Its page 5 Brooklyn column ran the police version under "Crap Shooter Shot by Policeman," without comment. On page 18, under a headline beginning "POLICEMAN USED," the paper described the friends' account as "a remarkable story that is quite different from the version the police have told," and relayed their brutality charge with the qualifier "if true."

accounts.label: Police version
accounts.gist: During a raid on a crap game one of the players attacked the officer with a knife (A1), or Hartgrave had a razor and slashed a detective (A2), and he was shot.

accounts.label: Hartgrave's friends
accounts.gist: The players ran when a plain-clothes man approached and Hartgrave went home; police broke in a door, dragged him about three houses down the street, and shot him while two held him, then clubbed him; he had no razor and did not resist arrest.

framing.detail: The brief 'Crap Shooter Shot by Policeman' gave only the officer's account (A1).

The follow-up called the friends' version 'a remarkable story' at odds with the police account and relayed their charge that police had been 'unusually brutal to Race people' in the neighborhood, with the qualifier 'if true' (A2, A3).
